title: Executive Security KPI Program — Overview
description: Landing page for the executive security KPI program. Every persona dashboard is built on the same 9-table data model, so a KPI on any one of them can be traced down to the same raw event, and every dashboard ties cyber posture back to revenue, net income, or IT budget.

viz_ds_impact_12mo.title: Financial Impact of Security Incidents (selected period)

viz_cyber_cost_pct_rev.title: Total Cyber Cost (incidents + fraud) as % of Revenue, Selected Period — the single number that ties this whole program to the P&L

options.markdown:
## Persona Dashboards

| CEO | CFO | COO | CIO |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise Cyber Risk & Resilience | Cyber Financial Exposure & Security ROI | Operational Resilience & Incident Response | Security Operations & Technical Risk Posture |
| Risk score, material incidents, customer trust, regulatory standing, cyber cost as % of revenue | Fraud loss, spend vs. loss avoided, regulatory fine exposure, revenue/net-income baseline | Availability vs. SLA, MTTD/MTTR, incident backlog, vendor ops risk, revenue at risk from downtime | Vulnerability management, SOC triage, patch compliance, MITRE ATT&CK, spend as % of IT budget |
| [Open CEO Dashboard](ceo_dashboard) | [Open CFO Dashboard](cfo_dashboard) | [Open COO Dashboard](coo_dashboard) | [Open CIO Dashboard](cio_dashboard) |

### How the drill-down works across all four dashboards

1. **Board KPI** — a single aggregated number (risk score, fraud loss, availability %, open vulnerabilities), several of which are already expressed as a share of revenue, net income, or IT budget.
2. **Business Unit** — click the KPI's breakdown chart to filter to one of 7 business units.
3. **System / Channel / Asset** — click again to narrow to the specific application, channel, or vendor.
4. **Event record** — the underlying incident, flagged transaction, vulnerability scan, or SOC alert row.
5. **Cross-dashboard join** — `business_unit` and `system` are shared keys across all 9 datasets, so a CEO-level incident can be traced to the CIO's SOC alert and vulnerability scan that caused it, or the CFO's fraud loss it produced — and `company_financials.csv` ties the whole chain back to revenue, net income, and IT budget. Every KPI here reacts to the Time Range picker above (each row's own date is filtered explicitly, since `inputlookup` results have no `_time` field for Splunk to auto-filter), except the point-in-time open-vulnerability count.

options.query: | inputlookup security_incidents.csv | eval _tf=strptime(date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | where _tf>=$tok_time.earliest$ AND _tf<=$tok_time.latest$ | fields - _tf | stats sum(financial_impact_usd) as total_impact

| inputlookup fraud_transactions.csv | eval _tf=strptime(date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | where _tf>=$tok_time.earliest$ AND _tf<=$tok_time.latest$ | fields - _tf | where is_fraud="Y" | eval net_loss=loss_amount_usd-recovered_amount_usd | stats sum(net_loss) as net_loss

| inputlookup uptime_availability.csv | eval _tf=strptime(week_start, "%Y-%m-%d") | where _tf>=$tok_time.earliest$ AND _tf<=$tok_time.latest$ | fields - _tf | stats avg(uptime_pct) as avg_uptime | eval avg_uptime=round(avg_uptime,3)
| inputlookup vulnerability_scans.csv | where (severity="Critical" OR severity="High") AND patch_status!="Patched" | stats count as open_vulns

ds_vulns_12mo.name: Open Critical/High Vulns (current, not time-picker scoped)

options.query: | inputlookup security_incidents.csv | eval _tf=strptime(date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | where _tf>=$tok_time.earliest$ AND _tf<=$tok_time.latest$ | fields - _tf | stats sum(financial_impact_usd) as impact | appendcols [ | inputlookup fraud_transactions.csv | eval _tf=strptime(date, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | where _tf>=$tok_time.earliest$ AND _tf<=$tok_time.latest$ | fields - _tf | where is_fraud="Y" | eval net_loss=loss_amount_usd-recovered_amount_usd | stats sum(net_loss) as fraud_loss ] | appendcols [ | inputlookup company_financials.csv | eval _tfq=strptime(substr(quarter,1,4)."-".printf("%02d",(tonumber(substr(quarter,6,1))-1)*3+1)."-01", "%Y-%m-%d") | where _tfq>=$tok_time.earliest$ AND _tfq<=$tok_time.latest$ | fields - _tfq | stats sum(revenue_usd) as revenue ] | eval total_cyber_cost=impact+fraud_loss, pct_of_revenue=round((total_cyber_cost/revenue)*100,2) | table total_cyber_cost, pct_of_revenue

ds_cyber_cost_pct_rev.name: Total Cyber Cost as % of Revenue
